newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Evicted Bosnian woman found dead in Mostar.
newsitem.headline: Evicted Bosnian woman found dead in Mostar.

text.p: A elderly, handicapped Moslem woman has been found dead in the Bosnian town of Mostar, two weeks after she was evicted from her flat in the Croat-held part of town, U.N. police monitors reported on Tuesday.
Rukija Bejtovic, 71, who was confined to a wheelchair, had been missing since Christmas Day when a Croat soldier took over her flat, a spokesman said.
"Yesterday afternoon the body of Ms. Bejtovic was found in an abandoned building in west Mostar," spokesman Alex Ivanko told reporters.
The cause of death had yet to be determined but U.N. human rights workers suspected Bejtovic may have died from exhaustion or hunger after being dumped in the abandoned building.
Ivanko said her body was being flown to the Croatian port of Split where an autopsy would be performed.
Croat thugs have been systematically expelling remaining Moslems from west Mostar over the past three months and stealing their property.
Mostar has been divided into Croat and Moslem sectors since a 10-month Moslem-Croat war which ended in 1994.
Diplomats say west Mostar is dominated by gangsters who have blocked international attempts at reunifying the city.

International police monitors, informed by a relative that Bejtovic was missing, visited her flat and found a Croat soldier and his family living there, Ivanko said. The front door lock had been damaged.
The Croat soldier said he bought the flat for 3,000 German marks ($1,900) but could not say who sold it to him.
Bosnian Croat military police detained the soldier but after 72 hours the militia had to release him because local police in western Mostar failed to press charges.
Ivanko said the United Nations was outraged by the release.
"These actions can only be described as criminal and disgusting beyond belief," he said.
